about: The closed list of physics material ids (AST-05, setup-asset-pipeline design decision 6, physics review R3). Every collision shape's 'material' and every material slot's 'physics' must be an id of 'materials', or 'surface:<id>' naming one of the thirteen ground surfaces (S01-S13, knowledge §7.2; their mechanics are physics' assets-src/surfaces.json) for a shape that stands in for ground; lib/meta.validate refuses anything else. New ids are added here with physics sign-off, never in a generator: the phase-1 sign-off is openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-18-p1-pipeline-hardening/review-materials.md. A plain id never shares a surface's name. The values are the physics engineer's to tune in phases 3 and 6.

fields.friction_static: mu_s of the drone's polymer parts on the dry material
fields.stiffness_n_per_m: contact compliance of the material under one touching part of the drone (a leg's foot, an arm, the body, the coil), in series with that part's own compliance; the contact law applies it to each part that touches, so four feet on it meet four times this; the rationale names the part it was derived for (the 15 mm reference foot unless it says otherwise) and the sink it gives; absent means rigid
fields.damping_ratio: zeta of that compliance; present with stiffness_n_per_m
fields.edge_radius_m: the radius the fiber bends over at a box's arris; a capsule, cylinder or sphere always uses its own radius, and a snag's radius_m overrides both; null means the material never carries an arris (it is only used on round shapes)
fields.break_stress_pa: optional: the bending rupture stress of a member on a capsule or cylinder; the contact law derives the break moment from the shape's own radius, M_b = break_stress_pa * pi * r^3 / 4, past which the shape stops resisting for the rest of the flight and a 'break' event is logged, and a hook snag of the material lets go at the same moment; absent means the member never breaks
fields.label: where the numbers stand: pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed
fields.rationale: the source or the calculation, as recorded in the physics review
fields.labelled value: p7a-ground's fields below are each labelled on their own, as drone.json's numbers and surfaces.json's are: {"value": <number or word>, "label": "pilot" | "measured" | "published" | "derived" | "assumed", "note": "<source, reason or formula>"}; a value labelled derived meets its formula or the loader refuses the file
fields.area_law: required on a row whose stiffness comes from a layer under a spread load (straw, fabric, sandbag): how the contact law scales stiffness_n_per_m from the 15 mm reference foot to a part's footprint (p7a-ground design 6): 'mat', a loose layer spreading the load 2:1 through its depth D, k = E_m·A_s/D with A_s the spread area at D and E_m = stiffness_n_per_m·area_reference_depth_m/A_s(reference foot); 'punch', an elastic flat punch, k in proportion to the footprint's equivalent diameter sqrt(4A/pi) (Sneddon 1965); 'winkler', a loose fill, k in proportion to the footprint's area
fields.area_reference_depth_m: with area_law: the layer's depth at which stiffness_n_per_m was derived for the reference foot; the mat law scales by it, and for the punch and winkler laws it names the layer the row was read for
fields.elastic_modulus_pa: required on bark and deadwood: the Young's modulus a slender member bends at as a cantilever from its root, k(x) = 3EI/x^3, I = pi·r^4/4, with x its chain length to the contact (p7a-ground design 6)
fields.wet: optional: what rain changes (Rain and Severe rain alike: a layer drains, so it is wet, never saturated): on a compliant row stiffness_ratio and the derived stiffness_n_per_m = the dry stiffness_n_per_m × stiffness_ratio; and friction_static, friction_kinetic, the clinging pull adhesion_pa (Pa, per wetted footprint) and its release separation adhesion_release_m (m), each labelled
fields.hardness_pa: p7f-damage: the indentation hardness of the face a blade meets (load over the indent's area, as Brinell's and the blade's ISO 2039-1 ball hardness read it), compared with drone.json's props.blade hardness_pa: a harder face is a hard target and the blade yields, a softer one is a soft target and yields to the blade (Rabinowicz's rule, p7f-damage design 5); a composite face's softer binder (a lower bound), a cellular one's (wood, rubber, foam) bulk. Labelled on its own: {"value": <number>, "label": <one of label's>, "note": <source or reason>}
fields.crush_strength_pa: p7f-damage: the pressure the material resists a blade carving it (a soft target's p_t, design 5); null where a blade passes the row without damage from it (a thin compliant row: its plants' cutting is the ground's elements, p7a-ground; fabric and mesh wrapping a prop are p7d-tether's); labelled as hardness_pa
fields.density_kg_m3: p7f-damage: the mass per volume a carving blade flings (m_f = ρ·V, design 5), of the material in the blade's path; labelled as hardness_pa

steel.label: assumed
steel.rationale: carried from surfaces-review §5 (polymer on dry mild steel, rolled or sawn edge); rigid per part: a 15 mm foot or an arm on a 40 × 2 mm tube meets its wall as a ring at ≈ 7e6 N/m (derived), far above a leg's own spring (2e4 N/m in the first attempt's probe, assumed), so a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) sinks under 0.01 mm and the part sets the bounce; a slender member's bending over its span (a 20 × 1.5 mm square tube over 1 m, 48EI/L³ ≈ 6e4 N/m) belongs to the shape, not this row

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: structural steel's Brinell 120–160 HB, 1.2–1.6 GPa (S235 to S355, the order p7f-damage design 5 cites); the softest grade's, so tubes, angles and rebar are above the blade for certain

crush_strength_pa.label: published
crush_strength_pa.note: S235's minimum yield, 235 MPa (EN 10025-2), as its compressive yield; harder than the blade, so the blade yields (design 5) and the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: steel, 7850 kg/m³ (EN 1991-1-1, Table A.4: 77–78.5 kN/m³)

sheet_metal.label: assumed
sheet_metal.rationale: carried: 0.5 mm corrugated sheet over a 1 m purlin span; per part: one part's load on mid-span, carried by a 0.2–0.3 m strip of an 18 mm sine profile (assumed), bends it at 4–7e4 N/m (48EI/L³, derived) and the crest dents under a 15 mm foot, so 2e4: a foot's 11.8 N share sinks 0.6 mm (1.2 mm at 25 N) and, in series with the leg, drums; its half-thickness edge cuts the fiber

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: a hot-dip galvanized sheet's outer zinc (eta) layer, 70 DPN, 0.69 GPa (American Galvanizers Association: eta 70, zeta 179, delta 244, the base steel 159 DPN), the softest layer a blade meets; a painted sheet's coat is thinner than a blade's chip and the steel beneath harder

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: the sheet's DX51D steel (EN 10346: tensile 270–500 MPa, no yield set; mills' 140–320 MPa), as its compressive yield; harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it, and a 0.5 mm sheet bends and dents long before (the shape's stiffness, not this row)

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: steel, 7850 kg/m³ (EN 1991-1-1, Table A.4); the zinc's 20 µm is a few % of a 0.5 mm sheet

timber.label: assumed
timber.rationale: carried; rigid per part: a 15 mm foot presses sawn softwood across the grain (E 0.3–0.9 GPa, the published radial and tangential ratios) as a punch of 5–16e6 N/m (E·b/(1−ν²), derived), so a foot's 11.8 N share sinks under 0.01 mm and the leg sets the bounce; a member that bends under a part is the shape's: a 50 × 25 mm batten over 0.6 m answers a foot at ≈ 1.4e5 N/m (48EI/L³, E 10 GPa), so a batten asset may override with ≈ 1e5 N/m

hardness_pa.label: derived
hardness_pa.note: red pine at 12 % moisture, the Wood Handbook's nearest to the region's sawn Scots pine (both hard two-needled pines of the same specific gravity order): side hardness 2,500 N (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) over the cap, 12.5 MPa; the Wood Handbook's side hardness is the load that embeds an 11.28 mm ball to half its diameter; over the cap's area π·D·D/2 = 199.9 mm² it reads as Brinell's and the blade's ISO 2039-1 hardness do (load over the indent's area)

crush_strength_pa.label: published
crush_strength_pa.note: red pine at 12 %: compression perpendicular to the grain, 4.1 MPa at the proportional limit (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a); a blade crushes a board's face across its grain (design 5's 4–10 MPa)

density_kg_m3.label: derived
density_kg_m3.note: red pine's specific gravity 0.46 at 12 % (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a): 0.46 × 1.12 × 1000 = 515

masonry.label: assumed
masonry.rationale: carried: brick, block, render; a worn arris; rigid per part: a 15 mm foot on brick (E ≥ 5 GPa, assumed) is a punch of ≥ 8e7 N/m (E·b/(1−ν²), derived), so a foot's 11.8 N share sinks under 1 µm and the part's own spring sets the bounce

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: brick, block and render: the binder of the mortar and render, the cement paste's softer hydrate, low-density C-S-H, 0.45 GPa by nanoindentation (Constantinides and Ulm 2007, J. Mech. Phys. Solids 55: 64–90), a lower bound for the face: its high-density hydrate (0.83 GPa) and the quartz sand and aggregate (Vickers about 11 GPa) are harder still; a lime binder's calcite and the fired clay body are harder too

crush_strength_pa.label: published
crush_strength_pa.note: a solid clay brick of grade M100, 100 kgf/cm² (GOST 530, the region's common grade); harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: a solid clay brick inside its published 1600–2000 kg/m³ (GOST 530's solid brick)

concrete.label: assumed
concrete.rationale: plastic feet on cast concrete sit in the published 0.5–0.7 band; a cast arris. Broken edges and rebar are 'edge' snags with their own radius. Also lifted asphalt slabs and kerbs (review-materials.md: 'asphalt' is a surface id only). Rigid per part: a 15 mm foot on concrete (E ≈ 25 GPa, assumed) is a punch of ≈ 4e8 N/m (derived), so a foot's 11.8 N share sinks under 1 µm and the part's own spring sets the bounce

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: the cement paste's softer hydrate, low-density C-S-H, 0.45 GPa by nanoindentation (Constantinides and Ulm 2007, J. Mech. Phys. Solids 55: 64–90), a lower bound for the face: its high-density hydrate (0.83 GPa) and the quartz sand and aggregate (Vickers about 11 GPa) are harder still

crush_strength_pa.label: published
crush_strength_pa.note: C20/25, its cube strength 25 MPa (EN 206), the order of cast slabs, kerbs and poles; harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: normal-weight concrete, 24 kN/m³ (EN 1991-1-1, Table A.1)

glass.label: assumed
glass.rationale: plastic on glass; a broken pane edge is a blade. Also glazed porcelain (insulators: cylinders, so the edge is their own radius). Breakability of a pane is a later plate model (review P3-6). Rigid per part: a 4 mm pane 0.5 m square bends under a 15 mm foot at ≈ 1.4e5 N/m (a simply supported plate under a centre load, E 70 GPa, derived), seven times a leg's own spring (2e4 N/m in the first attempt's probe, assumed), so a foot's 11.8 N share sinks 0.09 mm and the series stiffness differs by 13 %

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: soda-lime glass's Vickers hardness, about 5.5 GPa (the published order of float glass); glazed porcelain, the insulators, is harder

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: soda-lime glass's compressive strength in the glass makers' published 0.8–1 GPa; a pane breaks in bending first (a later plate model, review P3-6), and harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: soda-lime silicate glass, 2500 kg/m³ (EN 572-1)

cable.label: assumed
cable.rationale: carried; rigid locally, the span compliance comes from the wire geometry, T = w·L²/(8·sag): the row's span is a 12 mm bare stranded aluminium conductor (84 mm², 0.226 kg/m, derived from its T and sag; the top of L03's 7–12 mm medium class) on a 30 m street span (the short end of L03's 30–45 m) at L03's 2 % sag, 0.6 m, so T ≈ 416 N (knowledge §7.4, derived); per part at mid-span: a sideways push meets the taut-string 4T/L ≈ 55 N/m, so a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) swings the span P·L/(4T) = 0.21 m (derived; 0.20 m with the span's fixed length); a part pressing down also raises T, since the sagged span barely stretches: k = (T/L)/(1/4 − (3/16)/(1 + 12/λ²)) ≈ 200 N/m at small load (Irvine's linear theory, λ² ≈ 310 at an assumed E 60 GPa), stiffening as T rises, so the share sinks it 0.044 m (derived); the edge radius is the wire's own

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: the bare stranded conductor's aluminium 1350, its H18 temper's Brinell 42 HB (MakeItFrom, 1350-H18), 0.41 GPa; the conductor's hard-drawn H19 (ASTM B230) is at least as hard. Near the edge: 2.5 times the blade's, and an annealed 1350-O conductor, about 20 HB, would sit at 1.2

crush_strength_pa.label: published
crush_strength_pa.note: 1350-H19's yield, 170 MPa (MakeItFrom, 1350-H19: tensile 180 MPa), as its compressive yield; harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: aluminium 1350, 2705 kg/m³ (ASTM B230's density for its resistivity)

foliage.label: derived
foliage.rationale: per part: one 20 mm green branch at 1 m under it, E ≈ 10 GPa (published 8–12 GPa for green wood), I = πd⁴/64 = 7.85e-9 m⁴, k = 3EI/L³ ≈ 236 N/m, so a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) bends it 59 mm and four feet on four branches meet 800 N/m; ζ assumed for a leafy branch; the edge radius is the branch's own

hardness_pa.label: derived
hardness_pa.note: the branch's green wood: black locust (V01, the belt's tree), green: side hardness 7,000 N (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) over the cap: 35 MPa (derived; the Wood Handbook's side hardness is the load that embeds an 11.28 mm ball to half its diameter; over the cap's area π·D·D/2 = 199.9 mm² it reads as Brinell's and the blade's ISO 2039-1 hardness do (load over the indent's area)); an upper bound, since a young branch's juvenile wood, pith and bark and the leaves are softer

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: a thin compliant row: a blade passes it without damage from this row; the plants' cutting is the ground's elements (p7a-ground design 9, p7f-damage design 7)

density_kg_m3.label: derived
density_kg_m3.note: black locust's green wood: specific gravity 0.66 green (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) at a green moisture of 45 % (assumed: the Handbook's Table 4-1 gives white ash, another ring-porous hardwood, 44 % in its sapwood): 0.66 × 1.45 × 1000 = 957

elastic_modulus_pa.label: published
elastic_modulus_pa.note: black locust (V01's tree), green: the modulus of elasticity in static bending, 12.8 GPa (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a); clear wood, so a limb with its bark, pith and juvenile wood reads somewhat stiff, and a shrub's limbs (V13) take the same value until their species' is pinned

bark.label: assumed
bark.rationale: live trunks and limbs: furrowed or plated bark interlocks with a printed foot's layer ridges, so above sawn timber (0.45/0.35); the published 0.2–0.5 of polymers on wood is for planed faces, and bark is not planed; rigid per part locally: a 15 mm foot on bark and sapwood across the grain (E ≈ 0.5 GPa, assumed) is a punch of ≈ 9e6 N/m (derived), so a foot's 11.8 N share sinks under 0.01 mm; a slender member still bends as a cantilever from its root (a 30 mm limb at 1 m: 3EI/L³ ≈ 1.2e3 N/m at E 10 GPa), which the phase-7 contact law derives from the capsule chain, not this row (p1-v13-shrub review-physics N3); trunks and limbs are capsules, so the fiber bends over the member's own radius, never an arris

hardness_pa.label: derived
hardness_pa.note: live trunks and limbs, bark on green sapwood: black locust (V01, the belt's tree), green: side hardness 7,000 N (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) over the cap: 35 MPa (derived; the Wood Handbook's side hardness is the load that embeds an 11.28 mm ball to half its diameter; over the cap's area π·D·D/2 = 199.9 mm² it reads as Brinell's and the blade's ISO 2039-1 hardness do (load over the indent's area)); the furrowed outer bark crushes softer still

crush_strength_pa.label: published
crush_strength_pa.note: black locust, green: compression perpendicular to the grain, 8.0 MPa (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a); the outer bark yields first, so a blade carving a trunk meets the sapwood's bound

density_kg_m3.label: derived
density_kg_m3.note: black locust's green wood: specific gravity 0.66 green (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) at a green moisture of 45 % (assumed: the Handbook's Table 4-1 gives white ash, another ring-porous hardwood, 44 % in its sapwood): 0.66 × 1.45 × 1000 = 957

twig.label: derived
twig.rationale: the crown contact shell over the 5–10 mm twig cards (no capsules): per part, one 10 mm green twig 0.8 m long under it, E ≈ 10 GPa, I = πd⁴/64 = 4.91e-10 m⁴, k = 3EI/L³ ≈ 29 N/m, so a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) or a 20 N push goes 0.4–0.7 m through the shell to the branch capsules, which is the point; μ as foliage, ζ assumed lower for bare twigs; the fiber bends over the thinnest twig the shell stands for, radius 2.5 mm

hardness_pa.label: derived
hardness_pa.note: the twigs' green wood: black locust (V01, the belt's tree), green: side hardness 7,000 N (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) over the cap: 35 MPa (derived; the Wood Handbook's side hardness is the load that embeds an 11.28 mm ball to half its diameter; over the cap's area π·D·D/2 = 199.9 mm² it reads as Brinell's and the blade's ISO 2039-1 hardness do (load over the indent's area)); an upper bound for a twig's juvenile wood, pith and bark

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: a thin compliant row (the crown's twig shell): a blade passes it without damage from this row; the plants' cutting is the ground's elements (p7a-ground design 9, p7f-damage design 7)

density_kg_m3.label: derived
density_kg_m3.note: black locust's green wood: specific gravity 0.66 green (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a) at a green moisture of 45 % (assumed: the Handbook's Table 4-1 gives white ash, another ring-porous hardwood, 44 % in its sapwood): 0.66 × 1.45 × 1000 = 957

crown.about: what a crown's twig shell stands for (w9-village-physics 2.3, design.md '## 2.3'): the twigs a drone's part bears on, bending and breaking, and the leaves a turning blade flings and cuts; a variant not listed under leaf_area_density_m2_per_m3 draws no leaves

twig_length_per_volume_m_per_m3.label: assumed
twig_length_per_volume_m_per_m3.note: carried from PropStrikes.CrownTwigLength (w3-farmland-ground 2.7): about one 0.5 m axis of 5–10 mm twig per foliage spray, the sprays a card's half depth apart, 0.2–0.3 m³ each; the pipe model's check (Shinozaki 1964: a twig of section A carries a leaf area A·AL:AS, angiosperm branches 0.01–10 m²/cm² published, PROMETHEUS protocols; 0.1–1 taken, the twig 0.5 m long) gives 0.2–24 m/m³ of 7.5 mm twigs over the crowns' 0.21–2.09 m²/m³ of leaf (design.md 2.3)

twig_diameter_m.label: assumed
twig_diameter_m.note: carried from PropStrikes.CrownTwigDiameter: the middle of the shell's 5–10 mm twig cards

twig_free_length_m.label: assumed
twig_free_length_m.note: carried from the length density's note: one 0.5 m axis a spray; a part bears on a twig at an arm spread evenly over it (design.md 2.3)

twig_rupture_stress_pa.label: assumed
twig_rupture_stress_pa.note: green wood's modulus of rupture: 23–90 MPa over small stems' bending tests, lower toward the pith (search abstracts, not read in full; design.md 2.3); a twig is juvenile wood with pith and bark, so the lower half: 50 MPa. Green black locust's 95 MPa (the Wood Handbook, as this row's hardness cites it) is the upper bound

twig_elastic_modulus_pa.label: assumed
twig_elastic_modulus_pa.note: carried from this row's rationale (E ≈ 10 GPa, green wood); inside the 5.7–18 GPa of small stems' bending tests (search abstracts, design.md 2.3)

leaf_mass_per_area_kg_m2.label: published
leaf_mass_per_area_kg_m2.note: dry leaf mass per area of woody plants' leaves, 60 g/m² (26–251; shade 50.9, sun 90.7): Onoda et al. 2011, Table 1 (docs/reference-notes/stem-properties.md [2], §4's leaf row)

leaf_dry_matter_content.label: assumed
leaf_dry_matter_content.note: dry over fresh mass of a leaf (0.2–0.5 assumed, not looked up): the fresh mass a blade flings is leaf_mass_per_area_kg_m2 / 0.35 = 0.171 kg/m²; the needles of the pines are taken as leaves

leaf_work_to_shear_j_per_m.label: published
leaf_work_to_shear_j_per_m.note: work to shear across the lamina, 0.1 J/m (0.021–0.724; woody sun 0.127, shade 0.066): Onoda et al. 2011, Table 1 (stem-properties.md [2], §4)

leaf_critical_speed_m_s.label: derived
leaf_critical_speed_m_s.note: the edge's speed below which a leaf is pushed aside uncut: stem-properties.md §2.2's sharp-edge law for a leaf blade across its width, 37–51 m/s (derived there from Devee et al.'s 4.3–5.1 N and Onoda's lamina), its middle 44 m/s × the prop's edge factor 3 (PropStems.EdgeFactor, assumed 2–4) = 132

leaf_cell_m.label: assumed
leaf_cell_m.note: the size of the cube a disc clears of leaves where its plane passes: half a 10 cm leaf, the part of a leaf cut at the plane that leaves with the cut (the rest hangs from its petiole); numerical too (the cleared cells' store)

elastic_modulus_pa.note: dry hardwood's published 10–15 GPa at 12 % moisture (the Wood Handbook, Table 5-3a) derated by about a third for checking and decay, which take strength before stiffness: break_stress_pa is derated by about half, 40 MPa against the published 60–110 MPa

deadwood.label: assumed
deadwood.rationale: dead trees, broken tops, fallen branches, brush, logs, wattle rods: friction as weathered timber; rigid until it snaps at M_b = σ_b·π·r³/4 from the member's own radius (a 10 mm dead twig: 3.9 N·m, 8 N at a 0.5 m tip, so one foot's 11.8 N share snaps it), σ_b 40 MPa assumed under the published 60–110 MPa rupture of dry hardwood for checking and decay; locally rigid per part as bark, and a slender member bends before it snaps as bark's do (p1-v13-shrub review-physics N3); members are capsules, so the fiber bends over their own radius

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: dry wood as the timber row's 12.5 MPa (derived there), halved for checking and decay as the row's break_stress_pa halves the published rupture

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: the timber row's 4.1 MPa across the grain (Forest Products Laboratory 2021, Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, Table 5-3a, red pine at 12 %) halved for checking and decay, as break_stress_pa is

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: air-dry wood as the timber row's (derived there); decay lightens it by an amount not measured here

asbestos_cement.label: assumed
asbestos_cement.rationale: slate sheets and fragments: a cement-bound surface under a polymer foot, as concrete; a 5.8 mm 8-wave sheet (published) with E ≈ 15 GPa and I ≈ t·a²/2 per metre of 40 mm waves answers a foot over a 0.6 m batten span at ≈ 1e6 N/m, so it is rigid per part (a foot's 11.8 N share sinks 0.01 mm) and the leg sets the bounce; the edge is the sheet's half thickness; a landing loads a sound sheet to ≈ 0.4 MPa against a published rupture ≥ 16 MPa, so plate breakage is a crash case for a later plate model (review P3-6)

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: the sheet's cement matrix: the cement paste's softer hydrate, low-density C-S-H, 0.45 GPa by nanoindentation (Constantinides and Ulm 2007, J. Mech. Phys. Solids 55: 64–90), a lower bound for the face: its high-density hydrate (0.83 GPa) is harder, and the chrysotile fibres (Mohs 2.5–3) are of the binder's order

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: the cement matrix's compressive strength at a dense paste's order; the sheet breaks in bending first (published rupture at least 16 MPa, the row's), and harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: a fibre-cement sheet inside its published 1400–1800 kg/m³ order

area_law.label: assumed
area_law.note: loose straw spreads a part's load 2:1 through its depth (K§7.1 step 4, carried): k = E_m·A_s/D, so E_m = 490 N/m × 0.125 m / π(0.07 m)² = 3.98 kPa (derived) for the reference foot's spread disc, against the K§7.2 mat's 4 kPa; a half-skid lying along the face spreads over (0.22 + D)(0.01 + D) and meets 3.03 × the foot's stiffness on S04's mat (derived)

area_reference_depth_m.label: derived
area_reference_depth_m.note: S04's mat depth (assets-src/surfaces/S04_patch.json's mat_depth_m), the depth the 490 N/m was derived at

stiffness_ratio.label: assumed
stiffness_ratio.note: wet straw softens (the published direction: its modulus falls as it takes up water, Tavakoli et al. 2009) and a wet mat packs down; 0.6 (p7a-ground design 1)

stiffness_n_per_m.label: derived
stiffness_n_per_m.note: stiffness_n_per_m × wet.stiffness_ratio: a foot's 11.8 N share sinks 40 mm

friction_static.label: assumed
friction_static.note: wet straw grips a part harder: straw's friction on sheet metal and plywood rises with its moisture (Tavakoli et al. 2009, the published direction)

friction_kinetic.label: assumed
friction_kinetic.note: as friction_static, 0.1 under it as dry

adhesion_pa.label: assumed
adhesion_pa.note: wet straw clings: a tenth of wet soil's 3 kPa (surfaces.json's wetting.adhesion_wet_pa), since its stems touch a part along lines, not over a film (p7a-ground design 1)

adhesion_release_m.label: assumed
adhesion_release_m.note: a clinging straw lets go once the part has lifted about a straw's diameter

straw.label: derived
straw.rationale: thatch, hay, a stack, straw carried by a mesh or a roof: the belt_straw mat (modulus 4 kPa, surfaces.json) 0.125 m deep (S04's mat, re-measured unchanged) under the 15 mm reference foot, km = modulus·π(b/2 + D/2)²/D ≈ 490 N/m, per part as the ground mat's own law reads it: a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) sinks 24 mm and the 25 N reference foot 51 mm, under the 80 % cap of 0.1 m; μ and ζ carried from that mat; the fiber sinks into a straw edge, so the bend radius is the soil-lip figure 0.02 m (assumed); bundle ends are hook snags the generator writes. Straw lying on terrain is the surface's mat (surface:belt_straw's cover), never this id; a straw layer over a shape, a surface shape standing in for ground included, is this id (p1-s04-belt-straw review-physics §3).

hardness_pa.label: derived
hardness_pa.note: an upper bound: the wall's solid at three times wheat straw's published tensile strength, 21–31 MPa (O'Dogherty et al. 1995, J. Agric. Eng. Res. 62: 133–142; Tabor's H ≈ 3σ); a hollow stem collapses at a small fraction of it

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: a thin compliant row: a blade passes it without damage from this row; the stems' cutting is the ground's elements (p7a-ground design 9, p7f-damage design 7)

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: the bulk of the layer the row stands for (thatch, a stack, hay), between loose straw's tens and a baled stack's 130–200 kg/m³ (the published order)

area_law.label: assumed
area_law.note: a mattress or cushion answers a part as an elastic flat punch, whose stiffness grows with the punch's equivalent diameter (Sneddon 1965, published form), as the row's check against comfort foam reads it; a half-skid's 0.01 × 0.22 m footprint meets sqrt(2.2e-3/1.77e-4) = 3.5 × the reference foot's 160 N/m (derived)

area_reference_depth_m.label: assumed
area_reference_depth_m.note: the mattress or seat cushion the row was read for (the sheets' 0.1–0.2 m); the punch law has no depth, so it names the layer only

fabric.label: assumed
fabric.rationale: tarps, curtains, mattresses, sofas, seats, a canvas tilt, greenhouse film: a polymer foot on woven PE or canvas, above the published 0.2–0.4 of plastic on plastic for the weave; per part: the sheets' 50–100 mm sink of a mattress or seat is each foot's under its quarter of 4.8 kg (11.8 N), 118–235 N/m, so 160 N/m: a foot sinks 74 mm (55–100 mm over the 3.6–6.5 kg loadouts) and four feet meet 640 N/m (the 600 N/m read for the whole drone sank them 20 mm); checked as a flat punch into comfort foam of E ≈ 10 kPa (E·b/(1−ν²) ≈ 165 N/m; the published 25 % ILD grades of 10–30 lbf give 5–17 kPa) and as a slack tarp at T ≈ 100 N/m (assumed) over a 1 m span, 2πT/ln(a/r) ≈ 150 N/m under the foot; ζ for a damped cushion that does not bounce; the edge is a hem or a fold

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: the woven polyethylene or polypropylene of a tarp or a cover, inside those polymers' ball-indentation hardness, 40–80 MPa (the published order of their ISO 2039-1 data sheets); the cushion under it is far softer

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: a thin compliant row: a blade passes it without damage from this row; fabric wrapping a prop is p7d-tether's (p7f-damage design 5)

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: the cushion the row's stiffness was read for, polyurethane comfort foam inside its published 25–40 kg/m³ grades; a tarp's film is about 950

rubber.label: assumed
rubber.rationale: tyres: a polymer foot on tread rubber sits in the published 0.6–0.9 band; tread rubber (E ≈ 5 MPa, 10 mm) under the 15 mm foot compresses at EA/t ≈ 9e4 N/m and the carcass flexes under it, 5e4 N/m together, per part: a foot's 11.8 N share sinks 0.24 mm; ζ for rubber hysteresis; a tyre is a cylinder, so the fiber bends over its own radius, and 10 mm stands for a rubber box's rounded shoulder

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: tread rubber does not yield; its indentation pressure at a ball's depth is of its modulus' order, the row's E about 5 MPa (Shore A 60–70 tread)

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: tread compound's tensile strength inside its published 15–20 MPa order: a blade carving a tyre tears the rubber

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: a carbon-black tread compound inside its published 1100–1200 kg/m³ order

plastic.label: assumed
plastic.rationale: PVC frames, crates, housings, trim, bumper covers, packaging, EPS remnants: polymer on polymer in the published 0.2–0.4 band; rigid per part: the reference part is a 3 mm PP or ABS wall 50 mm across between its ribs or webs (assumed; a PVC profile's webs sit closer), which a 15 mm foot bends as a centre-loaded plate at 1.2–4.9e5 N/m (simply supported to clamped, E 1.3–2.4 GPa published, derived; the local punch E·b/(1−ν²) ≈ 2–4e7 N/m in series takes off about 1 %), so a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) sinks 0.02–0.1 mm and the series stiffness with the leg's own spring (2e4 N/m in the first attempt's probe, assumed) differs by 4–15 %, as on glass; past 55–100 mm between ribs a wall falls below five times the leg's spring and its bending is the shape's, not this row's: a 3 mm PP bumper cover 0.5 m across answers a foot at 1.2–4e3 N/m as a flat plate (derived; its curve only stiffens it), so the share sinks it 3–10 mm, and the car asset that carries one writes that as its own shape stiffness_n_per_m, as a timber batten does (the ≈ 1e2 N/m read before was a 0.1 m beam strip, which ignores the plate's two-way bending); a moulded edge 1–2 mm; EPS yields at 70–100 kPa (published grades): a foot's 11.8 N share presses 67 kPa and holds, the 141 kPa of the 25 N reference foot crushes it, a deviation accepted for remnants (review-materials.md)

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: PP, ABS and PVC-U inside their ball-indentation hardness, 60–130 MPa (the published order of their ISO 2039-1 data sheets), PVC-U the highest. Near the edge: 0.6 times the blade's, and a PVC-U frame up to 0.8

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: the compressive yield of PP, ABS and PVC-U inside their published 40–80 MPa; EPS remnants crush at 70–100 kPa (the row's)

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: ABS's 1050 kg/m³, inside PP's 905 and PVC-U's 1400 (the published densities)

mesh.label: derived
mesh.rationale: chain-link bays as thin boxes: a 2 mm galvanised mesh strung at ≈ 200 N/m (assumed) over a 3 × 1.5 m bay (Y03; conformal radius 0.95 m at its centre, derived) answers one part as a membrane, k ≈ 2πT/ln(a/r): r 0.05 m for an arm across the cells or the body's plates gives ≈ 430 N/m (a foot on one 50 mm cell, r 0.025 m, 350), so a part pushed at the drone's 47 N bows the bay 0.11 m and is caught, not bounced; three parts broadside meet 1300 N/m against 1100 for the whole drone as one load (r 0.3 m), so the per-part sum holds where the 800 N/m read for the whole drone did not; ζ assumed for link friction; μ as steel; the fiber bends over a 1 mm wire, a cut risk

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: the galvanized wire's outer zinc (eta) layer, 70 DPN, 0.69 GPa (American Galvanizers Association), as sheet_metal's: harder than the blade

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: a thin compliant row: a blade passes it without damage from this row; the mesh wrapping a prop is p7d-tether's (p7f-damage design 5)

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: the wire's steel, 7850 kg/m³ (EN 1991-1-1, Table A.4)

razor_wire.label: derived
razor_wire.rationale: concertina razor tape (F01): the coil body, a sagged coil and a trampled mat; μ as steel (the barbs hold through the turn records, not μ); one loop under a part as a ring under a diametral load, k = f·EI/((π/4 − 2/π)R³) with the 2.5 mm core (EI 0.383 N·m² at an assumed 200 GPa) and f = 2 for the crimped tape (assumed, 2–3.8): 57 N/m for a 0.90 m coil, so a drone on four legs meets about 240 N/m and sinks 0.20 m; a coil of another diameter writes its own shape stiffness_n_per_m = 60·(0.45/R)³; ζ assumed for loop-on-loop friction and the clips; the edge is half the published 0.5 mm blade; the core (7.4 kN at an assumed 1500 MPa) never breaks under the drone; the fiber ignores razor_wire shapes and bends over the turn records' edge_radius_m (review-physics.md of p1-fortifications-sheet)

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: the tape's steel at its cut barbs, as the steel row's (S235's 120 HB); its faces' zinc is 0.69 GPa and a stainless tape harder: harder than the blade either way

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: as the steel row's (S235's yield); harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: steel, 7850 kg/m³ (EN 1991-1-1, Table A.4)

area_law.label: assumed
area_law.note: the fill is a loose soil (the row's tamped 5e6 N/m³), Winkler's foundation, so the stiffness grows with the footprint's area: a half-skid's 2.2e-3 m² meets 2.2e-3/1.77e-4 = 12.4 × the reference foot's (derived)

area_reference_depth_m.label: derived
area_reference_depth_m.note: F04's filled bag, 0.12 m (the row's shoulder of a 0.12 m bag); the winkler law has no depth, so it names the layer only

sandbag.label: derived
sandbag.rationale: filled sandbags (F04): μ as fabric (a polymer foot on woven polypropylene or hessian, assumed); a 15 mm foot at 67 kPa punches into loose fill (surface bearing capacity 2–4 kPa), so the fill acts as a loose-soil row: tamped fill at 5e6 N/m³ (assumed, between tilled and meadow_sod) under the 15 mm reference foot, k = bearing·A = 884 N/m, so a leg sinks 13 mm static and 28 mm at 25 N; ζ from those rows' damping at a quarter of 4.8 kg, 0.94; the edge is the rounded shoulder of a 0.12 m bag (derived), so a line over a wall top never cuts; elastic, so no footprint stays (a deviation from the soil law, accepted); no wet adhesion on polypropylene (review-physics.md of p1-fortifications-sheet)

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: the woven polypropylene bag a blade meets first, inside polypropylene's ball-indentation hardness, 60–80 MPa (the published order of its ISO 2039-1 data sheets); the fill's quartz grains are far harder, and their sanding of a blade is the soil rows' (surfaces.json's sand share), which this row does not carry

crush_strength_pa.label: derived
crush_strength_pa.note: the sand fill's bearing, c·N_c = 1.04 kPa × 5.14 (dry sand's cohesion, Wong 2008, Theory of Ground Vehicles, Table 2.3; Prandtl's N_c); the bag's woven tape adds a cut, not a pressure

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: dry to moist sand inside its published 1500–1700 kg/m³ order

carbon_composite.label: assumed
carbon_composite.rationale: carbon-fibre laminate: the drone's own arms, plates, legs and skids (the Svinoriz 10 Opto model's collision, p5-drone; the drone side's contact material of the same id in drone.json, p6-flight-core 1.6) and any other cut carbon plate or roll-wrapped tube; signed off by physics in p7b-airframe (D-050's fit). A polymer part on the laminate's epoxy-rich face, as plastic on plastic in the published 0.2–0.4 band; rigid per part: the reference part is a 3 mm quasi-isotropic plate (E ≈ 50 GPa, ν 0.3, assumed) 0.09 m across between its supports (the drone's plates), which a 15 mm foot bends as a centre-loaded simply supported square plate, w = 0.0116·P·a²/D (Timoshenko's coefficient, published) with D = E·t³/(12(1−ν²)) = 124 N·m, at ≈ 1.3e6 N/m (derived), so a foot's 11.8 N share (a quarter of 4.8 kg) sinks 9 µm and the part's own spring sets the bounce; a roll-wrapped 10 mm tube is a cylinder, so the fiber bends over its own radius; a plate's milled edge, lightly sanded as builders do against cut leads and straps (assumed: a fresh milled edge is sharper still), bends the fiber over 0.5 mm

hardness_pa.label: assumed
hardness_pa.note: the laminate's epoxy-rich face over its carbon fibres: cured epoxy's macro hardness is of the blade's own order (Rockwell M about 100–110 against glass-filled nylon's about 100, the published orders), and the fibres a strike reaches past the face and at every milled edge are far harder, so harder than the blade. Near the edge: 1.8 times the blade's

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: a quasi-isotropic carbon/epoxy laminate's compressive strength inside its published 0.4–0.6 GPa order; harder than the blade, so the strike does not read it

density_kg_m3.label: assumed
density_kg_m3.note: carbon/epoxy at a 55–60 % fibre volume inside its published 1500–1600 kg/m³ order
